PROJECT_TITLE: DPSP III: Geothermal Power Generation Project
LONG_DESCRIPTION:
The Geothermal Power Generation Project targets additional renewable energy baseload generation to reduce Indonesia's reliance on coal. The project will provide financing for expanding geothermal power generation.

Output 1: Geothermal power plant constructed and commissioned. The project will support GDE in commissioning a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Dieng Central Java Province and a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Patuha West Java province.

Output 2: Institutional capacity of GDE strengthened. The project will strengthen GDE's capacity to plan for develop and operate geothermal power plants including management of complex technical conditions multiple coordinated contracts and environmental risks.

Output 3: Community development program enhanced. The project will support enhancement of GDE's Community Development Program through more strategic engagement with the communities and evaluation of programs that can most meaningfully contribute to improved well-being of nearby communities.

The Dieng subproject faces technical challenges and high-density of farming activities, the Patuha subproject is nearby to protected forest. As part of ADB's assistance the project will enhance health safety emergency planning and development programs for nearby communities. The project will ensure that there will be no impairment of high biodiversity value from forest clearing in critical habitat. These activities will serve as an example for how Indonesia's geothermal resource in similar geographic contexts can be developed without detriment to the existing surroundings.

The expansion of the two units will contribute to reaching Indonesia's renewable energy targets and contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in Indonesia and globally. Additional renewable energy supply will also prevent the development of equivalent fossil fired plants to meet growing electricity demand.

PROJECT_TITLE: DPSPIII: Indonesia Geothermal Resource Risk Mitigation Project (GREM)
LONG_DESCRIPTION:
This project aims at scaling up investment in geothermal energy development and supporting Indonesia in its efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the country.
The previous geothermal projects in Indonesia benefiting from the CTF supported construction of pilots (public) exploration drilling (public) and delineation drilling (public and private).

This project is building on the previous ones and has a dual focus of (i) providing risk mitigation to incentivize scaled-up investments by established developers as well as (ii) supporting new local developers to create a deeper market for geothermal development. This is expected to enable geothermal development at scale in the most cost-effective manner with substantial leverage of private developers' equity and adoption of private sector solutions and innovations in geothermal exploration drilling strategy and management for this operation.

This project has two components:
-Component 1 to mitigate risks in geothermal resource drilling supported through the establishment of a new financing facility, and
-Component 2 for technical assistance and capacity building.

CTF is expected to contribute to both components for an aggregate amount of USD 75 million as follows:
-Component 1: USD 72.5 million (out of which 20 for the public sector and 52.5 for the private sector),
-Component 2: USD 2.5 million (out of which 1.5 for governance and management to a state-owned non-banking financial institution PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (PT SMI) and 1 for technical assistance and capacity building to the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources MEMR National Electricity Company PLN and a public geothermal developer Geo Dipa).

In terms of instruments CTF is expected to contribute as follows:
-Component 1 (USD 32.5 million for the contingency recovery grant and USD 40 million for the loan):
?for the public sector: loan for exploration/delineation purposes, and
?for the private sector: convertible recovery grant for exploration purposes and loan for delineation purposes,
-Component 2: grant (USD 2.5 million).
This project is key for Indonesia highlighted as one of the Government's priority efforts in reaching the NDC. It has also been flagged by the World Bank as one of the flagship initiatives that will have a transformational effect in reducing carbon emissions by one of the biggest coal-dominated countries in the world.

PROJECT_TITLE: Rice-straw powered biowaste to energy
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This consortium, let by Carnot Ltd, seeks to develop the world's first profitable rice-straw bioenergy demonstrator for a rural community in Lombok Island, Indonesia. Rice straw is separated from the grains during harvesting and either combusted (producing CO2) or left to decompose (producing methane with 25\* Global Warming Potential) due to challenges with harvesting it, particularly in flooded paddy fields (a common occurrence). Straw Innovations has created innovative technology that overcomes the barriers to harvesting it in all weathers, unlocking a potential 300Mt of rice straw generated in Asia every year.Rice straw has high ash content (around 20%), comprising about 75% silica. This, combined with other components in the straw (chlorine, potassium) causes melting and slagging - fouling in boilers when combusted. Hence, it is not an easy fuel to chop or combust. PyroGenesys have developed a lower-temperature pyrolysis process which can convert rice straw into Biochar, a carbon-sequestering fertiliser that can be used by the rice farmers, and biofuel. The carbon sequestered can be traded on carbon removal markets. Surplus biofuel not used to generate electricity can be sold. Electricity is a low-value commodity and renewable electricity projects will typically require very large scale to be profitable and attract funding required from investors. PyroGenesys' process solves this problem by opening up two very high-value revenue streams.Carnot is developing ceramic engine gensets with double the efficiency of state-of-the-art diesel gensets, capable of operating on all fuels. These will provide electricity to the rice mills as their base load as well as electricity to a rural community. Integrating Carnot's gensets enables revenues generated by biofuel sales to be maximised.Indonesia:* Is the world's 5th largest GHG emitter.* Is the largest producer of biofuels worldwide.* Has mandated to convert a significant portion of its palm oil into FAME biodiesel.There is a reluctance to move to renewable energy due to fossil fuel sunk costs-subsidies and no proven profitable off-grid low-carbon energy business model. This demonstrator project aims to be the catalyst to breaking the deadlock and unleashing investment into Indonesia's enormous renewable energy potential.Key project outputs:* Pilot-scale demonstration of business model feasibility* 200,000kg rice-straw feedstock,* 76,000kg value-added-biochar-53,200kg carbon sequestration-80,000kg biofuel,* 2.28MWh electricity provided to rice mill.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SOLAR2WAVE: DESIGN OF FLOATING SOLAR FARMS TO OVERCOME TOUGH OCEAN WAVES
PROJECT_TITLE: Solar2Wave: Design of Floating Solar Farms to Overcome Tough Ocean Waves
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Indonesia has a population of approximately 273m, of which 1.5m still lack access to the energy grid. These people live on remote islands, relying on diesel power generation that is expensive and unreliable.The Solar2Wave project will carry out a floating photovoltaic (FPV)-based innovation to solve the energy-access issue of Indonesia's remote islands. An FPV farm is fully scalable, as it consists of small individual solar panels. Different sizes of FPV farms can be placed along the coastal line of an island and connected to residents. In particular, the Solar2Wave innovation can ensure that FPV panels remain intact from incident ocean waves, and thus provide a sustainable solution.By providing energy access to Indonesia's remote islands, Solar2Wave will bring improvements to the economy, working conditions, education, health services, and hazard resilience. This will be demonstrated through a case study based on a representative island.Following the present feasibility study, Solar2Wave will show the potential to be placed for ~6000 islands of Indonesia with residents. The innovation will make FPV an appealing solution to replace the country's current 88% electricity using fossil fuels. We can foresee a long-term development of FPV in Indonesia. The UK and Indonesia will benefit each other from the associated businesses. The enormous FPV market in Indonesia can be a golden opportunity for these two countries to establish joint corporations, and conduct extended trade as well as cultural and educational engagements.Eventually, Solar2Wave will be boosting the world's trend of extrapolating FPV from lakes to seas. The project will help us achieve the Net-Zero goal and mitigate climate change.

PyroGenesys' process solves this problem by opening up two very high-value revenue streams.Carnot is developing ceramic engine gensets with double the efficiency of state-of-the-art diesel gensets, capable of operating on all fuels. These will provide electricity to the rice mills as their base load as well as electricity to a rural community. Integrating Carnot's gensets enables revenues generated by biofuel sales to be maximised.Indonesia:* Is the world's 5th largest GHG emitter.* Is the largest producer of biofuels worldwide.* Has mandated to convert a significant portion of its palm oil into FAME biodiesel.There is a reluctance to move to renewable energy due to fossil fuel sunk costs-subsidies and no proven profitable off-grid low-carbon energy business model. This demonstrator project aims to be the catalyst to breaking the deadlock and unleashing investment into Indonesia's enormous renewable energy potential.Key project outputs:* Pilot-scale demonstration of business model feasibility* 200,000kg rice-straw feedstock,* 76,000kg value-added-biochar-53,200kg carbon sequestration-80,000kg biofuel,* 2.28MWh electricity provided to rice mill.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: RESULTS-BASED LOAN SUSTAINABLE AND RELIABLE ENERGY ACCESS PROGRAM WESTER
PROJECT_TITLE: Results-Based Loan Sustainable and Reliable Energy Access Program Wester
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The goal of the program is to achieve sustainable and reliable access to a reliable, modern electricity supply for the population and companies in the five target regions in West and Central Java. The program is structured as a results-based loan (RBL) and is being implemented in close cooperation with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which is acting as lead financier for the overall RBL program. The project executing agency is the state-owned energy supplier PT PLN. Java dominates Indonesia's economy, contributing 59% to the national GDP in 2020. Java is home to 111 million people, around 41% of Indonesia's 270 million inhabitants, and 34% (8.6 million) of the country's poor with an income of less than one USD per day.The program area is home to 47% of all Indonesian micro and small enterprises. Nationwide access to electricity is available, but frequent interruptions and power losses limit the security of supply. In order to achieve sustainable and inclusive economic growth, Java will need 259 TW of electricity by 2030, or 66.4°% of Indonesia's projected demand. In order to meet this demand and achieve the Indonesian government's ambitious targets for the expansion of renewable energies and the accelerated energy transition, Java's electricity grid must be strengthened. The program thus contributes to achieving the goals of the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP). The target group comprise private households and companies, especially MSMEs, in the program regions. The implementation structure of the RBL program is based on the achievement of specific results, on which the disbursement of funds is based. The achievement of objectives is reviewed annually by an independent consultant. Indicators are used to measure target achievement and set the corresponding disbursement, such as the annual reduction in power outages and their duration as well as the increase in procedures within PLN that comply with international environmental and social standards.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: HYBRID BIOMASS-SOLAR CELL DRYER FOR NUTMEG FARMER GROUP IN SUKARESMI, BOGOR-WEST JAVA
PROJECT_TITLE: Hybrid Biomass-Solar Cell Dryer for Nutmeg Farmer Group in Sukaresmi, Bogor-West Java
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The requested funding will be used to purchase a biomass-fueled oven dryer for nutmeg farmers in the village of Sukaresmi, located in the Bogor administrative district. Due to the high rainfall intensity in this region, the drying process of nutmeg seeds is considerably more difficult for the farmers. As a result, they are often forced to sell their product in a moist state at a much lower price. The oven dryer enables space-saving, weather-independent, and uniform drying of seeds, resulting in a higher product value upon sale.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: CLIMATE INVESTMENT FUNDS - ACCELERATING COAL TRANSITION INVESTMENT PROGRAM (CIF-ACT)/FONDS D'INVESTISSEMENT CLIMATIQUE - INITIATIVE POUR LA TRANSITION
PROJECT_TITLE: Climate Investment Funds - Accelerating Coal Transition Investment Program (CIF-ACT)/Fonds d'investissement climatique - Initiative pour la transition accélérée du charbon (CIF-ACT)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This project aims to accelerate the transition from coal-powered to clean energy while ensuring a holistic, integrated, socially-inclusive and gender-equal just transition in recipient countries: India, Indonesia, Philippines and South Africa for the first phase of the project. There could be more recipient countries in following phases. The Climate Investment Funds - Accelerating Coal Transition (CIF – ACT) investment program is building support at the local level to reconsider the development of new coal plants and accelerate the retirement of existing coal assets. It will foster new economic activities fueled by new clean energy sources for those impacted by the transition. The program works with public sector utilities and private sector operators to define pathways to advance transitions while ensuring the pursuit of a just transition approach in supporting a change away from coal in recipient countries. Project activities include: (1) supporting the closure and decommissioning of coal mines and coal power plants, (2) supporting power plant repurposing toward renewable energy and energy storage, (3) providing funding support for labour retrenchment packages and reskilling/retraining packages, including a gender action plan, and (4) developing a transition strategy as part of  implementing investment projects through close consultation with key stakeholders across different ministries and agencies within a recipient country.This project aims to benefit the communities in the CIF-ACT recipient countries, particularity workers affected by the coal-to-clean transition, including women and other traditionally marginalized groups such as Indigenous peoples, youth and persons living with a disability. PROJECT_TITLE: Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: P4I's goal is to contribute to 'quality infrastructure development that drives inclusive growth in Southeast Asia'. The end-of-investment outcome is 'Improved decision-making towards quality infrastructure underpinned by strong government-to-government partnerships'. P4I has three focus areas: planning and prioritisation of projects, implementation support for public infrastructure procurement, and sector policy and regulation. Climate change, gender equality and social inclusion are integrated throughout. P4I is delivered via four linked approaches: a quick response mechanism with high calibre advisers to provide advice at short notice to Southeast Asian governments and regional institutions, long term engagement through government-to-government partnerships, technical assistance that supplements and supports government to government partnerships, and regional networking and learning to bring together Australian experts with Southeast Asian counterparts.

The end-of-investment outcome is 'Improved decision-making towards quality infrastructure underpinned by strong government-to-government partnerships'. P4I has three focus areas: planning and prioritisation of projects, implementation support for public infrastructure procurement, and sector policy and regulation. Climate change, gender equality and social inclusion are integrated throughout. P4I is delivered via four linked approaches: a quick response mechanism with high calibre advisers to provide advice at short notice to Southeast Asian governments and regional institutions, long term engagement through government-to-government partnerships, technical assistance that supplements and supports government to government partnerships, and regional networking and learning to bring together Australian experts with Southeast Asian counterparts.

PROJECT_TITLE: Oxfam Australia
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The ANCP is a unique Australian aid program. It is a partnership between the Australian Government and accredited Australian NGOs. For over 40 years, this partnership has contributed to sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction in some of the world's poorest countries. The ANCP is the Australian Government's longest running and largest NGO program. The total value of the ANCP is $132.5 million in the 2019-20 financial year, of which Oxfam Australia will receive $10,125,709.00.
